title: Log it again: the meals you repeat, in one tap
intro: People stop logging food because it feels tedious, and logging often is what predicts results. In 145 recent App Store reviews rated one to three stars, 42 blamed a redesign that made logging slower and 15 named the paywalled barcode scanner. Most meals are repeats, so this makes them one tap and puts the diary back on the home screen. Camera tools stay Premium.

today.title: The diary sits below the summary
today.text: The home screen leads with totals, a Premium card and progress. The diary, used several times a day, is at the bottom behind “View all”.

today.title: Every save goes back to the top
today.text: One food at a time, and each save returns to the top of Today, as reviewers describe. Three foods means three trips.

proposal.title: Your usual meal, one tap
proposal.text: At 8 am the diary offers the breakfast you had on most recent mornings, with its items and total. Log it, or change it first.

proposal.title: Edits save where you are
proposal.text: Serving chips open under the entry and save as you tap. The screen doesn’t move.

proposal.title: Your foods first, no ads
proposal.text: The add sheet ranks your own foods by how often you log them. Barcode scan stays Premium, as one quiet line.

proposal.title: Copy a meal into the right slot
proposal.text: Copy one meal or a whole day from any recent day. Items keep their slots and amounts, and Undo is always there.

lessons: Put the most frequent job on the home screen. A summary can be one tap away; the daily task can’t.
Speed for repeat actions doesn’t need AI. The user’s own history is fast, cheap and already accurate.
Keep the user’s place. Sending people back to the top after every edit turns small changes into chores.
test: Does one-tap logging make people stop checking what they log, or stop seeing a reason to upgrade? If 3 of 5 testers say either, the idea needs rethinking.

compare.title: Logging the same breakfast again: before and after
compare.question: A free user eats the same breakfast most mornings: oats, a banana and a coffee. It’s 8 am. The same moment, two designs, both re-created in MyFitnessPal’s visual style.

before.try: Tap Log next to Breakfast and add Oats with milk (tap the name, then Add to Breakfast, or tap +). Now do the banana and the coffee.
before.notice: The diary sits below the calorie and macro summary. Each food is added on its own, and every save sends you back to the top of Today. The barcode scanner is Premium.

after.try: Tap Log breakfast. Then tap Banana and pick ½. Press Later and tap Copy on Lunch.
after.notice: The diary leads the home screen, the meal you repeat is one tap, and edits save in place. Scanning stays Premium, as a quiet option.
